_doc: port (the realism work, phase 5b, Track P: drop parties and the Seers' Party Room): where the parties are held, what a host's kit is made of, and the defaults chosen. Read by src/port/BotParty.ts. Every item is named by its 274 debugname (test/party.test.mjs checks each resolves).

venues: the F2P drop parties' three (the busiest of them at the start, by the bots within 60 tiles: never the human's place), and the members' Party Room in Seers' Village (its room box, chest, lever, Party Pete and the Seers' bank, measured on the 274 map: the research). `drop`: the middle of the 5x5 square the host drops in; `say`: how a bot names it.

kit: from the host's own bank (and pack), never bought: the stackables it drops one pile each (cheap runes, arrows, feathers); produce (logs, ores, bars, cooked fish, uncut gems: single items, or a note in the Party Room when one is worth under 100, which Pete leaves); gear of the metals named (bronze to black); 1 party in 10 one better item (a mithril or adamant piece, or 50 natures on members) within `betterMax`. Never a tool, a rare, an untradeable or (on a free world) a members item: those never reveal (Zone.revealObj) and the chest refuses them.

budget: the kit's value (port/BotPrices.itemValue) in coins, log-uniform in the range; drops: how many piles; coins: the share of the budget a coin pile is (now and then a joke pile of 1-10: 'lol 1 coin drop'). The lever: 1,000 coins (the knights' dance 500 more, 1 party in 4): a sink.

guests (the variety work, round 1, track F: ISS-3): each bot of the pool asked with chance joinChance[0] + joinChance[1] x its sociability (0.4 + 0.4 before: parties of 2-5); an asked guest busy at its moment is asked again every 20 ticks while it can still be there for the drop, then the next of the pool in its place; a full pack comes too (it drops a piece of junk for a pile, or watches); and at the build-up and the drop passers-by within 15 tiles walk in now and then (at most 8: 2004's drop parties drew whoever heard the calls).
